title: Using Bit-Masks / Manual Bit-Packing for Boolean Fields
pattern: Declaring boolean configuration flags inside a single primitive integer (`u8` or `u32`) and manipulating them via bitwise operators (`&`, `|`, `<<`) to save memory.
why_bad: Modern optimizing compilers automatically pack boolean structures efficiently. Manual bit-packing ruins readability, bypasses compiler type safety, and introduces bitwise CPU instruction overhead compared to normal structs with boolean fields [330].
detection: Struct fields manipulated via raw numeric bitwise masks or custom binary shift functions instead of clean struct access.
counterexample: Implementing low-level hardware device driver registers or custom network frame formats where exact bit structures are mandated by hardware. `Context-dependent`.
fix:
```rust
struct UserFlags {
    is_active: bool,
    is_admin: bool,
    has_pro: bool,
}
```
